headline: Honeywell commercialises University of Texas advanced amine solvent for CCS
summary: Gas to Power Journal reports Honeywell has commercialised an advanced amine solvent developed at UT Austin's Texas Carbon Management Program (Gary Rochelle's piperazine / potassium-carbonate chemistry, licensed to Honeywell in 2021) as a post-combustion capture offering for power, cement and steel flue gas, pitched to cut capture cost through higher efficiency and smaller equipment.
co2crc_note: Lower-cost post-combustion amine capture is directly relevant to CO2CRC's capture R&D and to industrial/power capture economics in Australia.
extractor_note: Article page not fetchable (org egress policy blocked all trade-news domains this run); date and gist confirmed via Google Alerts feed metadata plus corroborating web search. 'advent' in the source headline read as 'advanced' (Honeywell Advanced Solvent Carbon Capture).

headline: Mafix raises US$5.4m pre-seed to commercialise CO2-removing silicate fertiliser
summary: Seattle agtech Mafix closed a US$5.4m pre-seed round led by Azolla Ventures (with Astera Institute, Counteract VC, Impact Science Ventures and Plug and Play Ventures) to scale a Stanford-developed process that accelerates silicate-rock weathering into a silicon fertiliser, delivering enhanced-rock-weathering CO2 removal within a single growing season; funds will produce roughly 1,000 t of fertiliser for a commercial demonstration.
co2crc_note: Enhanced-weathering CDR is adjacent to CO2CRC's geological-storage focus; a watch-brief on the widening CDR investment landscape rather than a core storage development.
extractor_note: Carbon Pulse (the feed source) is paywalled and egress-blocked; the figure and details are corroborated via Carbon Herald and AgNavigator, both dated 20 Aug 2026.

headline: Chester Zoo says proposed CO2 pipeline's impact would be 'unacceptable'
summary: Chester Zoo has objected that a proposed CO2 pipeline crossing land it manages for wildlife would cause unacceptable environmental impact - compounded by the nearby HyNet CO2 pipeline already under construction - with both routes feeding CO2 to storage beneath Liverpool Bay; a social-licence flashpoint for UK CCS transport infrastructure.
co2crc_note: Community and environmental opposition to CO2 pipeline routing is a live social-licence precedent for Australian CCS transport and storage permitting.

headline: Alberta's stored CO2 tops 18 million tonnes
summary: EnergyNow reports cumulative CO2 stored across Alberta's CCS operations (Shell's Quest and the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line) has surpassed 18 million tonnes, framed as evidence of the province's carbon-capture leadership - a retrospective aggregate milestone rather than a discrete new event.
co2crc_note: Cumulative-storage milestones are useful comparators for Australia's own storage-volume messaging (e.g. Moomba, Gorgon).
extractor_note: Cumulative aggregate figure (18 Mt total, not annual Mtpa) so capacity_mtpa left null; retrospective milestone placed under 'Still on the radar', not a discrete in-window event. Page egress-blocked; date from feed.
